comparability: All runs ingest raw feeds into a newly created persons index and fresh pipeline container. Host cache was warm and ES container reused for tuning. Timings vary; these are not repeated cold-cache hardware-normalized comparisons. Later Redis and final default follow-ups start fresh ES containers with existing data volumes and warm host input cache. Redis adds an unconstrained coordinator with eight organization loaders and shared in-memory staging; the adjacent local follow-up used three staging producers inside the pipeline quota; the current default uses four. Later CPU/RAM experiments reuse ES, preserve mapping and request durability, and add exact cgroup CPU counters; all eight experiments are also grouped in bench/cpu_ram_trials.json. Later LMDB codec tuning uses the preserved pre-optimization image and candidate in A/B/A/B order, starting a fresh isolated Elasticsearch volume for the first control and reusing ES thereafter. Full records are grouped in bench/lmdb_trials.json; dictionary preparation is included in every candidate staging time. Later sorted-prefetch A/B/A/B trials use the current Zstd baseline and retain the disabled default; all measurements are in bench/prefetch_trials.json. Final submission verification after provider waiver used fresh isolated ES/staging volumes and disabled prefetch; it is not a controlled tuning comparison. Timing-fix verification uses the same defaults with high-resolution duration measurements and fresh isolated ES/staging volumes; no performance gain is inferred.
